Compare latent classes on an external outcome

Source: R/three-step.R
three_step.Rd

three_step() estimates differences in an external outcome between latent classes defined by a previously fitted model. It addresses whether classes distinguished by their indicator patterns also differ on a variable that was not used to identify them. The measurement model remains fixed, so the outcome comparison retains the original meaning of the classes.

Latent class membership is inferred rather than observed. Assigning each observation to its most probable class and comparing the resulting groups treats those assignments as certain, which can distort estimated outcome differences. Three-step methods address this problem by using classification-error probabilities from the fitted model when estimating class-specific outcome means. The default Bolck–Croon–Hagenaars ("bch") method applies correction weights; the alternative maximum-likelihood ("ml") method incorporates the classification-error probabilities into a model for the outcome.

The analysis provides estimated outcome means within classes or differences between pairs of classes, together with standard errors and confidence intervals. Pairwise differences can also be tested against zero, with adjustment for multiple comparisons. For supported multilevel models, comparisons may concern individual profiles or group classes. Uncorrected modal-assignment and posterior-weighted analyses are available as additional methods.

Usage

three_step(
  x,
  data,
  outcome,
  level = c("individuals", "groups"),
  method = c("bch", "proportional", "modal", "ml"),
  ci_level = 0.95,
  contrast = c("none", "pairs"),
  adjust = c("BH", "holm", "hochberg", "hommel", "bonferroni", "BY", "none"),
  vcov_type = c("cluster", "independent"),
  variance = c("varying", "equal")
)

Arguments

x

A covariate-free fit from multilpa() (family = "profiles", the default) or from lta() with its default homogeneous first-order transitions and invariant measurement, or a trajectory model that classifies persons (mixture_regression() with class_level = "group", with or without random effects) fitted without membership covariates. Fits with membership covariates and multilevel growth mixtures (cluster) raise latents_unsupported_three_step: the correction uses a fixed, unconditional classification-error matrix and independent units. The other families of multilpa(), lta() fits from the general transition engine (occasion-varying, second-order or covariate transitions, occasion-specific measurement, a stayer class, ordinal or count indicators) and mixture regressions with observation classes raise latents_unsupported_three_step too.

data

The data frame carrying the outcome, in the fit's row order. Columns shared with the fit are checked row by row; a frame with too little identifying information raises a warning that alignment cannot be verified. For a trajectory model it must be the data frame the model was fitted to.

outcome

Name of a numeric outcome column, without missing or infinite values, that is not a measurement indicator of x. For level = "groups" it must be constant within each group, and for a trajectory model within each person.

level

"individuals" (default) relates the outcome to profiles, "groups" to group classes. For a trajectory model the outcome is related to its person classes, reported with level = "persons"; "groups" is refused there with latents_bad_argument.

method

"bch" (default) applies the Bolck-Croon-Hagenaars weights; "ml" fits the maximum-likelihood step-three model (see Details); "proportional" weights by the posterior probabilities without correction for classification error; "modal" uses the uncorrected modal assignment, for comparison.

ci_level

Confidence level for the intervals (default 0.95).

contrast

"none" (default) reports one outcome mean per class; "pairs" reports the difference between every pair of classes, with a test against zero.

adjust

Multiplicity correction across the pairwise differences, passed to stats::p.adjust(): "BH" (default), "holm", "hochberg", "hommel", "bonferroni", "BY" or "none". Ignored for contrast = "none".

vcov_type

"cluster" (default) sums the influence contributions within the fit's groups and treats the groups as the independent units, as required when the outcome is measured on observations nested in groups. "independent" treats every observation as an independent unit, which is appropriate only when observations can be treated as independent. The choice is recorded in the result's vcov_type attribute.

variance

For method = "ml": "varying" (default) estimates a variance of the outcome in each class, "equal" one variance shared by the classes. Given with another method it raises latents_bad_argument.

Value

A base data.frame. For contrast = "none", one row per class with the columns level, method, class, estimate, standard_error, conf_low, conf_high and effective_n; class means are not tested. For method = "ml", a variance column (the outcome's estimated variance in the class) comes before effective_n, which is then the expected number of units in the class under the step-three model; the variance attribute records the choice. For contrast = "pairs", one row per pair of classes with the columns level, method, class, reference_class, estimate (the mean of class minus the mean of reference_class), standard_error, statistic, p_value, p_adjusted, conf_low and conf_high, as in r3step(). A contrast with zero or missing standard error has NA_real_ statistic and p-values.

The result's vcov_type attribute records the variance used; for contrast = "pairs" the adjust attribute records the correction applied to p_adjusted.

Details

On an lta() fit, level = "individuals" uses one row per occasion and relates the outcome to the profile at that occasion, with the default group-clustered variance accounting for the repeated occasions within a group. This is a marginal profile-outcome analysis, not a model of outcome effects on transitions or of a sequence-level outcome.

The cluster-robust variance is the sum of one outer product per independent unit, scaled by the small-sample (CR1) factor G / (G - 1) for G units (groups, or observations under vcov_type = "independent"). These contributions sum to zero at the estimate, so the variance has rank at most G - 1: it is zero with a single group and singular with as many groups as classes. Both cases raise latents_too_few_groups; vcov_type = "independent" gives the unclustered variance. For the same reason a class carried by a single unit (all its weight in one group, or under vcov_type = "independent" in one observation; Kish's effective number of carrying units below 1.5) has no standard error, whichever the method: its standard error, its interval and those of the contrasts involving it are NA, with a latents_small_classes warning.

With method = "ml" the assigned class is an indicator of the true class whose error probabilities are those of step one, and the outcome is normal within each true class. The log likelihood sum_i log sum_t pi_t D[t, W_i] phi(z_i; mu_t, sigma_t) is maximised over the class means and variances by EM followed by Newton steps, with the class sizes pi_t fixed at the average posterior probabilities and the classification errors D fixed, as in Latent GOLD's step-three model for a dependent variable. Multiple initialisations are used because the likelihood may have several local maxima. Equal-variance fits additionally use bounded BFGS optimisation from quantile-based initial values; accepted solutions must converge, have a sufficiently small score and yield a positive-definite information matrix. These searches do not guarantee the global maximum. Twenty random starts use a fixed internal seed, and the caller's .Random.seed is restored. R's hidden Box-Muller normal cache cannot be restored; see base::Random. Standard errors use a sandwich covariance estimator, clustered as for the other methods. As described above, a class supported by a single independent unit has no standard error. Maximum-likelihood estimates depend on the assumed within-class outcome distribution. Skewness or an incorrect equal-variance constraint can bias estimated means; BCH is less sensitive to these distributional assumptions (Bakk and Vermunt, 2016).

Because uncertainty in the estimated classification-error probabilities is omitted, interval coverage can be below the nominal level, particularly when classification is uncertain.

Interpretation

Correction for classification error depends on the fitted measurement model and assumes that the outcome and assigned class are independent conditional on latent class membership. The maximum-likelihood method additionally assumes a normal outcome distribution within each class. Reported uncertainty is conditional on the estimated classification-error probabilities and does not include uncertainty from estimating those probabilities or selecting the class solution. Outcome differences describe associations; they do not establish causal effects of class membership.

References

Vermunt, J. K. (2010). Latent class modeling with covariates: two improved three-step approaches. Political Analysis, 18, 450–469. Bakk, Z., Tekle, F. B., & Vermunt, J. K. (2013). Estimating the association between latent class membership and external variables using bias-adjusted three-step approaches. Sociological Methodology, 43, 272–311. Bakk, Z., & Vermunt, J. K. (2016). Robustness of stepwise latent class modeling with continuous distal outcomes. Structural Equation Modeling, 23, 20–31.

Examples

set.seed(11)
group <- rep(seq_len(40), each = 10)
truth <- 1L + as.integer(runif(400) > 0.5)
example_data <- data.frame(
  g = group,
  a = rnorm(400, ifelse(truth == 2L, 1.1, -1.1)),
  b = rnorm(400, ifelse(truth == 2L, 1.1, -1.1)),
  y = rnorm(400, ifelse(truth == 2L, 10, 0))
)
fit <- multilpa(example_data, c("a", "b"), "g", n_profiles = 2,
                n_group_classes = 1, n_starts = 4, seed = 1)
three_step(fit, example_data, "y")
#> Distal outcome by class (bch, 95% CI)
#> 
#> Class    Mean            95% CI    SE  Effective n
#> -----  ------  ----------------  ----  -----------
#>     1  -0.069  [-0.463,  0.325]  0.20       182.74
#>     2   9.972  [ 9.531, 10.412]  0.22       170.37
three_step(fit, example_data, "y", contrast = "pairs")
#> Distal outcome: class differences (bch, 95% CI)
#> 
#> Class  vs  Difference         95% CI      p  p (BH)
#> -----  --  ----------  -------------  -----  ------
#>     2   1       10.04  [9.37, 10.72]  <.001   <.001
